results.corrected_title: OpenAI and Cisco launch Shirudo, an open-source eBPF runtime for shielding live Linux systems
results.corrected_summary: OpenAI and Cisco launched Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps operators protect running Linux systems while a patch is tested and rolled out, with no restart needed. It uses eBPF programs called shields to observe suspicious activity and apply targeted protections. In a controlled Java4Shell test, a Codex-generated shield blocked an exploit against a running Elasticsearch process.
key_facts: Shields are eBPF programs; one in the Java4Shell test was generated by Codex
Shields are cryptographically signed and verified before loading
Operators can test a shield before enforcing it

results.corrected_title: Ant Group's Robbyant open-sources LingBot-Touch, a cross-sensor tactile foundation model
results.corrected_summary: Robbyant, Ant Group's embodied-AI unit, released LingBot-Touch, an open-source tactile foundation model. It maps signals from magnetic, visual and piezoresistive sensors into a shared representation. It was pretrained on nearly 5,000 hours of real-world tactile data. Across 26 real-world tests on two dexterous hands, four action models gained roughly 14 to 26 percentage points in average success rate with tactile input.
key_facts: Pretrained on nearly 5,000 hours of real-world tactile data
26 real-world tests on Sharpa Wave and XHand hands
